intent: Original game art; existing enemy sheet used only to preserve identity

prompts.cards: Create a production GAME UI TEXTURE ATLAS for an original refined-pixel-art post-apocalyptic survival shooter, Wasteland Echo. One square 1536x1536 image, EXACT regular grid of 3 columns and 2 rows. Each cell is 512x768 and holds one whole portrait card front inset by 12 pixels, no cropping or touching cells. Transparent background in gutters and outside card silhouettes. These are empty upgrade card FRAMES, not illustrations, not a mockup with typography. All card faces must have large clean light parchment areas for text overlay, no letters, no numbers, no icons, no UI labels baked into image. Expert detailed pixel art with restrained 2px/3px pixel clusters, rich wear, warm directional highlights, sharp pixels; NOT simple flat rectangles, NOT vector design, NOT generic glowing sci-fi borders. Tactile scavenger field workshop aesthetic: worn paper dossiers, cloth binding, chipped enamel, copper fasteners, stamped blank tabs. Six distinct layouts in reading order: 1 orange-brown gunsmith work order with charred leather spine and brass clips; 2 medical field record with faded oxblood cloth corner and stitched bandage pocket; 3 teal patrol map record with canvas straps and weathered compass-shaped corner hardware; 4 olive scavenger inventory ticket with torn paper edges and patched tool-pocket binding; 5 rare prototype engineering folio with aged brass corner brackets and restrained turquoise inlays; 6 veteran masterwork dossier with red wax seal hardware, double paper layers and old bronze reinforcement. Same underlying layout for every card: blank low-detail header zone y=5-12%; broad EMPTY inset artwork bay y=15-45% with subdued dark olive cloth backing; blank cream title zone y=48-57%; blank cream stat/body zone y=59-84%; blank bottom register strip y=89-96%. Decorative detail strictly confined to outer 7% perimeter and corners. Distinct silhouettes, bent corners and uneven repaired edges, realistic tiny pixel stitches/scratches and layered paper depth. Keep central text areas quiet and readable. No center illustration, no repeating crude box lines, no glow, no hands, no weapons. Orthographic front view, each card entirely visible, grid spacing precise. This is one coherent six-frame atlas for integration into an existing game.
prompts.icon-a: Draw a single cohesive production SPRITE ATLAS of 16 original detailed pixel-art upgrade objects for a post-apocalyptic scavenger survival shooter. Square canvas, EXACT 4 columns by 4 rows uniform grid. Transparent background, NO grid lines, NO labels, NO words, NO lettering, no surrounding cards, no hands, no character bodies. Each cell contains ONE clearly isolated object, centered with generous equal padding of at least 12% cell width, no touching neighboring cells. Objects rendered as high quality 96x96 pixel inventory illustrations enlarged with nearest-neighbor: crisp deliberate pixel clusters, stepped edges, controlled tiny highlights, 16-24 colors per object, dark warm outline, warm light upper-left, worn brass/olive steel/cloth/rust, restrained teal energy accents. Not crude geometric icons, not flat vector, not soft painterly render. All objects readable as distinctive physical scavenged equipment, suitable to display at 96-144 game pixels. Reading order row1: 1 oversized armor-piercing bullet with red pressure band and copper seams; 2 intricate automatic weapon bolt/gear with spring and alternating ratchet teeth; 3 dual-barrel branching gun action with two feed rails; 4 pointed tungsten dart penetrator with a cutaway casing. Row2: 5 twin copper induction rails with tiny teal coils; 6 thick reinforced gun breech with ribbed jacket; 7 scratched optical target monocular with red crosshair lens; 8 pair of teal-strapped weathered running boots. Row3: 9 field medical satchel with clean bandage roll and worn red cross patch; 10 horseshoe electromagnetic salvage magnet with copper windings; 11 olive ballistic vest with layered metal plates and visible straps; 12 a glass nanomed injector with green fluid and brass fittings. Row4: 13 patched scavenger coin pouch with mixed salvage coins spilling out; 14 quilted protective fabric swatch with copper mesh and teal insert; 15 an extendable melee weapon handle with locking collars and wrap; 16 grenade blast-shaping collar with four angled fins and amber core. Composition is a regular 4x4 sprite sheet, not a showcase scene. Each item is different and richly detailed at actual small pixel scale. Entire silhouettes visible. Alpha outside each object. Do not copy any existing game's icons.

One object per cell, all centered and fully inside their cells with 12% transparent margin. NO text, no symbols that look like lettering, no grid lines, no cards, no characters, no hands. Reading order: Row1: 1 miniature folding defense turret blueprint model made of brass gears and olive plates; 2 maintenance kit with a wrench, oil bottle and copper spring; 3 battered ammunition drum with red pressure gauge for continuous fire; 4 armored survivor belt with layered plate and fabric padding for enduring vitality. Row3: 9 salvaged small turbine generator with copper coils and teal vent; 10 a mechanical short-range contact relay with prominent jaws and amber sensor; 11 precision optical targeting goggles with one red lens, one cracked dark lens and frayed strap; 12 three connected copper electrode cartridges with a short zigzag cyan arc. Same light from upper left, muted earthy palette, visual variety of contours and materials, richer than simple rectangular code icons. Keep all sixteen silhouettes separated and fully visible. This is one coherent atlas for direct extraction into a game, not a concept art board.

prompts.weapons: A production 4x4 WEAPON SPRITE SHEET for an ORIGINAL refined-pixel-art wasteland survival shooter. Exactly sixteen equal square cells in a square canvas. Thirteen weapon sprites in reading order, cells14,15,16 EMPTY transparent. All weapons strictly horizontal SIDE VIEW, pointing RIGHT, orthographic 2D, no isometric perspective, no scene, no hands, no fingers, no arms, no sleeves, no floating shadow, no text, no labels, no frames. Each weapon fully inside its cell, at least 10% margin; weapon's barrel shaft horizontal and centered in each cell. All rendered like excellent hand-crafted 80x48 pixel game weapon art enlarged with nearest-neighbor: deliberate sharp pixel clusters, dark 1px outline, multiple muted steel shades, selective bright edge pixels, grip wrapping, screws, copper seams and mechanical cutouts. Rich detailed pixel art, NOT a few colored rectangles, NOT blurry painting, NOT futuristic generic white gun. Palette weathered olive steel, dark gunmetal, brown leather, restrained rusty brass, tiny turquoise/orange functional accents. Row1: 1 prismatic pulse rifle with narrow emitter muzzle, exposed twin copper power rails, polygonal focusing chamber and a teal crystal capacitor; 2 heavy slag grenade launcher, short fat ribbed barrel, vent holes, distinct cylinder, brown wooden stock and chunky trigger grip; 3 saw-disc launcher with toothed steel disc housed above its front receiver and a visible launch slit pointing right; 4 echo military saber with wrapped brown hilt at left and long slightly curved steel blade to right, brass guard and very narrow teal fuller. Row2: 5 shock warhammer, long wrapped shaft to right with heavy vertical steel hammer head on RIGHT, inset capacitor and cracked amber ceramic; 6 ratchet crossbow with open bow limbs at right, taut visible string and guide rail, arrow groove, wood/steel grip at left; 7 frost projector with ceramic insulated nozzle, two pale-blue coolant bottles, frosted copper piping and olive grip; 8 breach spear, long brown wrapped horizontal shaft and faceted narrow triangular steel spearhead on RIGHT. Row3: 9 rusty broad-bladed battle axe, long shaft left, curved bearded axe head at RIGHT, chipped silver cutting edge; 10 ash flamethrower, copper fuel cylinder below receiver, ribbed heat shield, orange pilot nozzle at right and black hose; 11 arc repeater, two copper electrode prongs at right muzzle and a small blue coil on dark gunmetal receiver; 12 compact knuckle blade, leather cuff on left, battered brass knuckle guard and two short forward steel talons pointing right. Row4: 13 long scavenger scythe, wrapped shaft extending to right with a clear crescent hooked blade at RIGHT tip, rusted spine and pale steel edge, entirely horizontal equipped orientation; 14 empty;15 empty;16 empty. Preserve distinct silhouettes, component construction, strong wood versus metal material contrast. Each item must look convincingly constructed and polished at small game scale. Transparent alpha background.
prompts.death-a: Make an animation SPRITE ATLAS for the FIRST FOUR enemies in the attached reference sheet. Reference only: top row contains drifter (blue ragged jacket), runner (lean red-brown shirt), spitter (green swollen belly), brute (large dark armored hunched humanoid), left to right. Preserve each exact visual identity, garment colors, face proportions and refined compact pixel-art style. The bottom row of the reference is NOT needed for this sheet. Output a square sheet with EXACT 4 columns and 4 rows, sixteen isolated frames, transparent alpha, no text, no grid, no background, no particle effects, no blood puddles, no detached body parts. Row1 drifter, row2 runner, row3 spitter, row4 brute. FOUR distinct sequential DEATH action drawings per row, left to right: frame1 lethal-hit recoil leaning backward while still upright; frame2 knees buckle, body falls sideways toward the RIGHT; frame3 body lands fully on its right side, limbs clearly bent, head and torso lowered almost to ground; frame4 settled horizontal side-lying corpse, slightly relaxed, eyes dimmed. A real drawn change of anatomy between frames, not four rotations of the same upright sticker. Feet contact baseline y=80% within each square cell in frames1/2, fallen torso rests at y=75-85% in frames3/4. Keep all frames at the SAME SCALE within each row and retain visible body/head volume; do not shrink the fallen body. Side three-quarter top-down 2D game view matching reference. Pixel art at about 72x72 logical pixels per frame enlarged nearest neighbor, crisp stepped outlines, nuanced ragged cloth and metal edge pixel highlights. Leave at least 10% margin from all cell edges, use compact poses that never cross cell boundaries. All characters face right before falling. Non-graphic restrained infection horror, no gore. This atlas is for runtime death animation continuity, so consistent clothing, anatomy, scale, baseline and frame order matter more than decorative detail.
prompts.death-b: Production DEATH ANIMATION sprite atlas for the BOTTOM FOUR enemies in the attached reference sheet, NOT the top row. Preserve their exact identity and compact refined pixel-art aesthetic. Reference bottom row left to right: screecher (dark purple ragged cloak and huge open pale jaw), crawler (low crawling brown mutant with elongated arms), warden (tall red coat/hood, dark helmet, angular faceplate and antenna), iron colossus (bulky brown-grey scrap armored robot/giant with visible orange chest furnace). Output square transparent-alpha image, EXACT regular 4 columns x 4 rows, one character action per cell. Row1 screecher, row2 crawler, row3 warden, row4 iron colossus. Columns are four sequential distinct drawings: 1 lethal hit recoil, still alive-looking but off balance, facing RIGHT; 2 body collapses to the right, knees/front limbs folding; 3 body lands on its side, low horizontal posture; 4 settled dead side-lying pose with relaxed limbs and dim eyes, and colossus furnace becoming dark. For crawler, first frame is its original low crouch, second forelimbs buckle, third rolls onto side, fourth relaxed side-lying. Do not turn crawler into an upright human. For the colossus preserve its distinct armored construction and orange furnace, no flesh or gore. Real anatomical pose drawings, not rotations of one standing sprite. Keep character SCALE and garment/armor details stable across columns. Constant ground baseline near 88% cell height; all objects fully in each cell with 8-12% padding, no overlapping cells. The original warden must remain red coated, screecher purple, crawler brown, colossus dark rust/steel. No text, no labels, no grid lines, no blood puddles, no detached limbs, no effects, no scenery. Sharp 72x72 logical-pixel character designs enlarged nearest-neighbor, dark outline, earthy shadows, upper-left warm edge highlights, crisp pixel clusters. Final settled poses should clearly read as fallen enemies, not shrunk upright stickers.
